elements.scope_reason: Flowchart branch criteria leading to 'Dental abscess likely': previous/current tooth pain with pus in mouth (continued in p54-7f0f7151).
elements.problem: Two issues. (1) 'Previous/current tooth pain': only a current 'Toothache' is matched; a patient whose tooth pain has settled but who now has pus/swelling would not satisfy the rule. SNOMED has the qualifier value 'Previous' (and 'In the past'), so (or Toothache (Toothache qualifier Previous)) was expressible and would need its own check_for entry. (2) Logic: the page reads 'tooth pain with pus in mouth, swelling next to tooth'. The rule requires toothache AND pus AND swelling. The comma list is ambiguous; the more clinically natural reading is tooth pain with either sign (an abscess that has not pointed shows swelling without visible pus). Requiring all three makes the rule stricter than the page. 'Pus' (morphologic abnormality) at 'Oral cavity structure' is an acceptable rendering of 'pus in mouth'; no precoordinated concept exists.

rule_level_problems.problem: Requires toothache AND pus in mouth AND swelling next to tooth. The page's 'tooth pain with pus in mouth, swelling next to tooth' is a comma list that more plausibly means tooth pain with either sign; a swollen, unpointed abscess (no visible pus) will never be called probable. Consider (and Toothache (or Pus@Oral cavity Swelling@Tooth/gum)).

'Previous/current tooth pain' is encoded as current Toothache only. SNOMED has the qualifier values 'Previous' and 'In the past', so a (Toothache qualifier Previous) alternative was expressible and would need a matching check_for entry.

The page's explicit escalations for a diagnosed abscess ('Refer same day if > 65 years, alcohol/drug misuse, HIV, diabetes'; 'refer urgently if ... temperature >= 38 °C') have no priority evaluation anchored on (active_condition Dental abscess). The red box only covers fever when swelling is also present. Borderline under the no-manage-tasks policy, but these are priority decisions, not treatment.

summary: The red box is fully and correctly encoded: trigger, fever-plus-swelling (three sites), unable to eat/drink, and spontaneous/night tooth pain all match the page with existing concepts, and every check_for item is consumed. The main weakness is the dental abscess rule, which demands toothache AND pus AND swelling where the page's comma list more plausibly means pain with either sign, and which ignores the page's 'previous' tooth pain despite a usable 'Previous' qualifier. The page's post-diagnosis escalations for abscess (same-day referral if > 65, alcohol/drug misuse, HIV, diabetes; urgent if fever) have no priority rule, which is borderline under the no-management policy but is triage logic the page states explicitly.
